info.title: Mycelium Fabric — Functional Data Service API
info.summary: Platform data surrounding a SysML v2 model: organizations, projects, membership, ownership and reviews.
info.description:
The REST surface of the Mycelium Fabric Functional Data Service: the platform data
that surrounds a SysML v2 model, rather than the model itself. Projects, branches, commits and model
elements belong to the Concurrent Server and are reached through the OMG Systems Modelling API; a
reference held here to anything on that side is an identifier, never embedded content.

Generated from the Enterprise Architect model `SysML2_Software_Architecture.qea`, in which every
operation is a `«route»` on an `«apiModule»` class. Five conventions follow from that and are not
visible in the paths:

- **Authentication and authorization happen at the edge.** Every request passes an nginx
  `auth_request` subrequest to `/internal/auth`, which answers 200, 401 or 403 and stamps the
  resolved account onto the request it allows. No operation below declares 401 or 403, because the
  gate produces them for all of them uniformly, and no operation takes a current-user parameter.
- **A body never nests a composed child that has routes of its own.** A project body carries no
  members, ownerships, reviews or protection rules; each is created and deleted through its own
  path. The one exception is a project's policy, which has no routes and is therefore nested.
- **A read can widen to the graph around it.** Every `GET` returning model data accepts
  `includeReferenced` and `includeComposed`. With neither set the response is the resource itself;
  with either it is a flat array of `Thing`, discriminated by `@type`, holding the resource first and
  then everything it references and/or composes, each once.
- **Every failure carries an `Error`**, the body defined by the OMG Systems Modeling API PSM, so a
  client reads errors from either server identically.
- **Server-assigned values are `readOnly`.** Identifiers and the audit stamps are omitted from
  request bodies and present in responses. A `PATCH` body is partial, so it is described by a
  separate `…Patch` schema with nothing required.

Collections are unpaged, deliberately: the expected volumes do not warrant it.

Operations carry `x-satisfies`, listing the Software System Specification requirements they
implement. Sixteen of the forty-six have none, which is accurate rather than an omission: the
specification does not cover reviews or comments at all, and the gate, session and policy-read
operations are architectural.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: The nginx auth_request target, answering 200, 401 or 403 and stamping the resolved account onto the request it allows.

tags.name: Session
tags.description: The single call a client makes when it opens a session.

tags.name: Organizations
tags.description: The organization tree and its membership, including user creation since a user cannot exist outside an organization.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: The project and everything composed into it except reviews, which have their own module.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: The mirror of a Keycloak identity, which is readable here but owned there.

tags.name: Reviews
tags.description: Merge proposals on a project and the comment threads they carry.

parameters.description: The request being checked, forwarded by nginx because the auth subrequest carries neither the original uri nor its method.

parameters.name: X-Original-Method
parameters.description: The verb the action is inferred from; the auth subrequest itself is always a GET.

200.description: Success.

403.description: The account may not perform the action.

200.description: The organizations, or the Things they include when an include parameter is set.
The organization, or the Things it includes when an include parameter is set.
The organization.

delete.description: Composition carries the delete down to the policy and to every project beneath.

200.description: The organization members, or the Things they include when an include parameter is set.

post.description: Refused when the user is already a member of the organization.

patch.description: Refused when it would leave the organization without an administrator.

200.description: The organization member.

delete.description: Removing the last member or the last administrator is refused, because an organization is modelled as having at least one of each.

200.description: The organization policy, or the Things it includes when an include parameter is set.
The organization policy.

post.description: Scoped to an organization, because a user is modelled as belonging to at least one.
The requesting user becomes the project administrator, and the policy is created with the project.

get.description: Scoped by visibility, so a public project appears across organizations.

200.description: The functional projects, or the Things they include when an include parameter is set.
The functional project, or the Things it includes when an include parameter is set.

patch.description: Carries the lifecycle, the mode and the policy flags, so the handler authorises each field rather than the route.

200.description: The functional project.

delete.description: Composition carries the delete down to the policy, the members, the ownerships, the reviews and the protection rules.

200.description: The branch protection rules, or the Things they include when an include parameter is set.

put.description: The whole set is replaced, since nothing references a rule by identity. Refused when two rules protect the same branch.

requestBody.description: The complete rule set for the project.

200.description: The branch protection rules.
The project members, or the Things they include when an include parameter is set.

post.description: Refused when the user is already a member of the project, or when an outside collaborator would be made administrator.

patch.description: Transferring administration and reassigning an ownership are both changes to the membership. Refused when it would leave the project without an administrator, make an outside collaborator administrator, or activate an ownership the member does not hold.

200.description: The project member.

delete.description: Removing the last administrator is refused.

200.description: The ownerships, or the Things they include when an include parameter is set.
The ownership.

delete.description: Refused while a member is still assigned to it.

200.description: The reviews, or the Things they include when an include parameter is set.

post.description: Both branches live in the Concurrent Server, so only their identifiers are held here. Refused unless the target branch is protected and every reviewer is a project member.

200.description: The review, or the Things it includes when an include parameter is set.

patch.description: Carries the status and the reviewer set, so submitting, approving and requesting changes are all status changes. Refused unless every reviewer of an open review is a project member.

200.description: The review.

delete.description: Composition carries the delete down to every comment thread.

get.description: Replies are identified rather than nested; includeComposed brings them into the same response.

200.description: The comments, or the Things they include when an include parameter is set.

post.description: A quote is a comment carrying the message it quotes; a reply is posted on the comment's own replies route.

patch.description: Resolving a comment is a status change.

200.description: The comment.

delete.description: Composition carries the delete down to the replies.

200.description: The replies, or the Things they include when an include parameter is set.
The reply.
The session.
